summary: External webhook confirmation delayed during multi-region fanout causing duplicate function-side effects
description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed duplicate side-effects (duplicate downstream payments and duplicate job dispatches) when using function-calling with an external webhook confirmation flow. The application fans out function call completions to a third-party webhook endpoint in multiple regions via our webhook fanout feature.

Impact:
- Two customers reported doubled transactions within a 2-hour window (FinSaaS staging -> prod migration).
- Duplicates are intermittent (~1 in 1,200 requests) but high severity for finance workloads.

Environment:
- Customer: FinSaaS Inc. (enterprise)
- SDKs in use: python-sdk v1.8.3 (server worker), ts-sdk v1.9.0 (edge orchestrator)
- Platform: Redwood hosted prod, multi-region fanout (us-east, eu-west)
- Model: rw-3.8b-chat pinned in config

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Client issues function call that triggers external webhook fanout to third-party payment processor.
2) SDK sends funcall request with idempotency token in X-Redwood-Id header.
3) Webhook endpoint experiences a transient spike (100ms->1200ms processing) in eu-west resulting in delayed 200 OK confirmation.
4) SDK (python worker) does an automatic retry after ack window expires (default 750ms configured by customer on worker pool).
5) Downstream processor receives two separate POSTs; their payloads are semantically identical but have slightly different Redwoods request ids and the idempotency header is missing in the second POST due to proxy rewrite on the eu-west edge.

Expected behavior:
- Client retry should not produce duplicate external side-effects when webhook confirmation eventually succeeds; idempotency token should be preserved end-to-end or the platform should suppress duplicate fanout if confirmation arrives late.

Actual behavior:
- Duplicate side-effects observed when confirmation latency exceeds client ack window and one of the edge routes strips or rewrites the X-Redwood-Id header.

Logs/IDs attached:
- Customer request ids: rwd-cust-20260314-9a1, rwd-cust-20260314-9b2
- Edge traces: trace-us-2247, trace-eu-7832
- Slack thread: #support-fintech (link provided in related_confluence_pages)
comments: 2026-03-14 09:12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer opened after noticing duplicate payments. Provided request ids and stack traces. Asked for SRE input on edge header rewrite behavior.

2026-03-14 10:03 - Miguel Santos (SRE): Confirmed intermittent header drop on eu-west edge for multipart/form-data fanout paths when proxy layer performs canonicalization. Reproduced locally with a synthetic fanout and slow webhook responder.

2026-03-14 13:27 - FinSaaS Ops (customer): Noted that setting client ack window to 2s reduced duplicate rate but did not eliminate duplicates. Asked whether platform can guarantee 'at-most-once' semantics for webhook fanouts.

2026-03-15 08:41 - Miguel Santos (SRE): Shared temporary mitigation steps (disable auto-retry for funcalls or increase ack window). Opening linked PR in SDK to add stronger header preservation and optional server-side dedupe for webhook fanout. See related_github_prs.
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis:
- The root cause appears to be a race between client-side retry driven by ack-window expiry and an edge proxy path that rewrites/sanitizes headers for multipart fanout routes. When the second request loses the idempotency header, downstream sees it as a distinct invocation.

Evidence collected:
- Packet traces show the original request arriving at eu-west with X-Redwood-Id present. The same request, when re-sent by the sdk-backed worker, goes through the us-east edge route for that retry and passes through a different sidecar that normalizes header casing and drops unknown headers for multipart content.
- Router logs (trace-eu-7832) include a 502 transient between edge and webhook, followed by a successful 200 for the re-sent request.
- SDK logs: python-sdk v1.8.3 shows a retry at +820ms after initial send due to ack timeout configured at 750ms by customer. ts-sdk orchestration logs show coordinated fanout to two regions; eu-west returned late.

Candidates for fix:
1) Server-side dedupe for webhook fanout using a canonical idempotency token computed from body+signature when X-Redwood-Id missing.
2) Ensure edge proxies preserve X-Redwood-Id for fanout routes and stop header canonicalization on multipart paths.
3) Expose SDK option to mark particular funcalls as "external-confirmation-required" and disable automatic retries for those calls, leaving retry responsibility to application logic.
4) Increase default ack window in our python-sdk for enterprise worker pools or make it configurable from Console per-route.

Related artifacts:
- Local reproducer: synthetic slow-webhook script + fanout test corpus (internal repro link in INT-412).
- Slack thread: #support-fintech (internal)
workaround:
Short-term mitigation steps provided to customer:
- Set the ack window to 2500ms on server worker pool (python) to reduce accidental retries.
- Disable automatic retry for funcalls that fan out to external payment processors.
- Add a per-call idempotency token in the webhook body payload (in addition to X-Redwood-Id) so downstream can dedupe when headers are missing.
These are documented to the customer; they reported fewer duplicates after increasing ack window but requested a platform-side fix for hardened at-most-once behavior.
resolution: In Progress: engineering is preparing a two-part fix: (1) edge proxy config change to stop header canonicalization for multipart fanout routes, and (2) server-side dedupe on webhook fanout that falls back to body-signature-based idempotency when header absent. ETA for staged rollout: 2026-03-22.
